page.layout: One column of running text, with Greek and Hebrew phrases inline. No marginal notes on this page. The far-right strip belongs to the facing page and is left out.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~12 letters] trabibus vero fornicem subjecit ex eadem materia, eumque in laquearia expolitum cum juncturis aureis. Iftæ trabes Josephi ad ipsa superiora laquearis pertinent: sed cætera verba inferiorem contignationis faciem concavam & ornatam nobis depingunt: quàm superiora illa tigna (de quibus supra) exhibebant. Deinde his omnibus impolita coaxatione, tandem addiderunt ⁵ [illegible, ~5 letters] crustam supremam: quam ideo è Vitruvio nucleum appellari non inconcinnè arbitror; quia ipso teste nucleus è testa tusa & calce similive materia constat (quamvis supremo loco, ut hîc, eum non collocet.) Constat autem è Gemara codicis Baba Metsja, [illegible, ~3 letters] olim ex istiusmodi vel non absimili materia fieri solitam. Gemarae ad cap. 10. cod. Baba Metsja hæc sunt verba (quamvis alii secus legant) [illegible, ~9 letters], quid est mahaziva? R. Chanina inquit; Calami, spinæ rubi (vel fracturæ) & lutum. Quæ à R. Nathane explicantur per [illegible, ~6 letters], calamos, (vel, si mavis, coria) spinas (aut segmenta) calcis effossæ minutias (nam hujusmodi calcem dari, dicique [illegible, ~3 letters] tradunt Heb.) & rudera. In Gemara quidem additur sententia Resch Lakisch, qui [illegible, ~2 letters] asseres esse dixit: verum id earum regionum respectu dixisse fertur, ubi contignationis suprema crusta ex asseribus fieri consueverat. R. Chaninam aliquatenus sequitur Maimonides; nec non Isacides in Baba Bathra, cum cap. 2. explicat [illegible, ~3 letters] sequ. verbis: [illegible, ~9 letters], Esterich) lingua Germanica, tectorium pavimenti; ille vero [illegible, ~2 letters] esse inquit, [illegible, ~9 letters], calcem lapidesque quos contignationi imponunt: (quibus Bartenora lutum addit, i. מיט.) Quod enim de lapidibus (quos R. Chanina & R. Nathan non recensent) hi affirmare videntur; de fragmentis & ruderibus accipi queat: priores autem illi calamos seorsim adhiberi non tradunt; sed proculdubio ubi calamos sive arundines cum luto & calce conjungunt lutum paleatum sive argillam arundinibus quisquiliisque subactam, eique similem qua parietes cratitii lutantur, significare volue-

page.notes: Greek line at the top and the Hebrew words inside the text are printed in small, worn type and are not legible letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The "ct" in "junctu-ris" is a ligature in the print. The reference mark ⁵ has no matching note on the page. The "i. מיט" in the parenthesis is Hebrew and is transcribed as printed only where readable. The page starts mid-sentence, so the first paragraph continues from the previous page.
